answer: Waakye is a Ghanaian dish made by cooking rice and beans together, often with dried sorghum leaves that give the grains a reddish-brown colour. It is widely eaten as a street-food breakfast or lunch and commonly served with stew, pepper sauce, eggs, fish, vegetables or gari. The accompaniments vary by cook and location.

facts.fact: Waakye consists of rice and beans cooked together.
The Rice Today account dated 1 March 2013 describes waakye as nationally popular Ghanaian street food.
The documented UN Tourism recipe begins cooking black-eyed beans and leaves before adding rice.
Rice Today lists eggs and vegetable, fish, chicken or beef stews among serving options.
Graphic Online explains that sorghum-leaf extract contributes colour to waakye.
Food & Wine published Zoe Adjonyoh's account of the layered waakye street-food plate.
